name: Cisco Meraki
description: Cisco Meraki MX, MS, and MR. Dashboard-first troubleshooting with optional Meraki Dashboard API calls.
notes: Meraki devices do not expose a full local troubleshooting CLI. Use Dashboard or the API.
API calls use the MERAKI_API_KEY environment variable so the key is never stored in a runbook.
Find the device serial in Dashboard > Devices.

categories.name: Dashboard
categories.description: Guided checks in the Meraki Dashboard.

workflows.title: Device uplink and latency
workflows.summary: Read WAN uplink state and recent loss/latency history for an MX.

steps.instruction: In Dashboard, compare the live uplink status under Security & SD-WAN > Monitor > Appliance status.

notes: An empty array usually means the device has not reported that telemetry yet.

workflows.title: Clients recently seen
workflows.summary: List clients and their recent usage for a network.

steps.instruction: In Dashboard, open Network-wide > Clients and filter by the client MAC or IP.

workflows.title: Site-to-site VPN status
workflows.summary: Check VPN peers, tunnel status, and recent alerts in Dashboard.

steps.instruction: Open Security & SD-WAN > Monitor > Site-to-site VPN.
Check the peer status, last change, and the tunnel latency for the affected subnet.
Compare the advertised local and remote subnets; an overlap silently prevents traffic from using the tunnel.
Open the MX's event log and filter for VPN or connectivity events during the failure window.

notes: Meraki VPN status is primarily a Dashboard workflow; API coverage varies by organization.

workflows.title: Packet capture from Dashboard
workflows.summary: Capture traffic on an MX from the Dashboard and download the pcap.

steps.instruction: Open Security & SD-WAN > Monitor > Appliance status > Tools > Packet capture.
Choose the interface, source, destination, protocol, and port. Keep the capture short.
Start the capture, reproduce the flow, stop it, and download the pcap.
Analyze the pcap against the MX flow and the upstream device counters.

notes: Captures are short-lived in Dashboard. Do not leave them running.

workflows.title: Switch port troubleshooting
workflows.summary: Inspect MS port status, PoE, VLAN, and errors.

steps.instruction: In Dashboard, open Switch > Monitor > Switches and select the port. Check status, PoE, VLAN, and errors.
Compare the port configuration with the upstream device and the endpoint's negotiated speed.

workflows.title: Wireless client troubleshooting
workflows.summary: Find an MR client and inspect its AP, signal, and connection history.

steps.instruction: In Dashboard, open Wireless > Clients, select the client, and check RSSI, SNR, retries, and the AP it is using.
Open the AP's RF profile and compare channel utilization with neighboring APs.

workflows.title: Organization alerts and events
workflows.summary: Review recent organization alerts and security events during the failure window.

steps.instruction: Open Organization > Alerts and filter by the affected network and time window.
Open Network-wide > Event log and filter for the device, client, or VPN event type.
For security events, open Security & SD-WAN > Monitor > Security center.

workflows.title: Validate Dashboard API access
workflows.summary: Confirm the API key and list organizations.
notes: A 401 means the key is invalid or expired. Never paste an API key into a ticket.
